subject: Post-demo: Medexa shortlist + prioritized model slate and risk asks
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@medexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Medexa demo recap + recommended model shortlist (quick read)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the three-model slate we recommend for the pilot/eval you asked for. I kept this tight so Ops and Procurement can run it forward.

TL;DR recommended shortlist (prioritized for staged evaluation):
1) Redwood-Atlas-70B (FP16) — baseline for highest quality on long-context document understanding (best F1 on our MedTech QA prompt-set).
   - Pros: top quality, robust on long clinical notes and table extraction.
   - Cons: higher cost (est. $1.10 / 1M tokens hosted), p95 gen latency ~420ms @ 256-token bursts on gpt-class GPUs.
2) Optima-30B (INT8) — middle ground: strong quality with significant cost savings.
   - Pros: ~70–85% of Atlas quality on our Medexa evals, cost ~ $0.35 / 1M tokens, p95 ~220ms.
   - Cons: slightly more sensitive to prompt engineering for tabular prompts.
3) Reach-13B (8-bit quant) — lowest-cost candidate for high throughput routing.
   - Pros: low cost (~$0.08 / 1M tokens), very low p95 latency (~90–120ms), good for short summarization/alerts.
   - Cons: observable drop for long-context QA and hallucination on edge-case legal text.

Why this mix: you mentioned two core workloads — (A) long clinical note summarization + question answering (quality-sensitive), and (B) short monitoring/alert summarization where cost and latency matter. The Atlas/Optima/Reach slate lets you run parallel evals and then route production traffic based on policy (quality-first for QA, cost-first for alerts).

Key evaluation artifacts attached and linked: prompt-pack-medexa-v1.zip (prompt variants + guardrail examples), benchmark-medexa-500k.csv (raw token-level results), and an eval dashboard link (Redwood Evals — Medexa 2/2026).

Quality/regression concerns we flagged in-demo:
- Long-context hallucination baseline: Atlas is strongest but we still see ~3% answer deviation on 8–12k token prompts; we recommend adding a high-precision reranker and a short answer verifier in the pipeline.
- Prompt brittleness on table extraction: Optima needs two additional prompt-patterns (see prompt-pack) to match Atlas on structured extraction.
- Canary thresholds: recommend 2–4% quality delta guardrails for rollback.

Suggested next steps (I’ll coordinate):
- You: confirm which 2-week window works for the evaluation (we have capacity week of 2/23).
- Redwood: we’ll provision the three models in a private pilot project, seed with the prompt-pack, and run the 500k-token bench.
- Procurement: if you want committed capacity for Optima/Atlas pricing, Ben is CC’d to pick up the commercial path.

If useful, we can add a Dedicated capacity quote for Optima with a burst buffer (reduces p95 by ~18% at 99th percentile).

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0147

Attachments: prompt-pack-medexa-v1.zip, benchmark-medexa-500k.csv

Looping in initial commercial math for a 3-month pilot (ballpark). These are preliminary — will finalize after we confirm traffic mix and whether Medexa wants Dedicated capacity.

Ballpark pricing for 30M tokens/mo (split 60% Optima / 40% Reach run-rate):
- Hosted (no commit): Optima ~ $0.35 / 1M tokens, Reach ~ $0.08 / 1M tokens => est. $9.8k/mo (total)
- 3-mo committed Dedicated discount (30% commit): est. $6.9k/mo equivalent (includes modest burst buffer)

If Atlas is included for any sustained QA traffic, add Atlas @ $1.10 / 1M tokens — a single Atlas-backed regression run (3% of traffic ~0.9M tokens/mo) would add ~$1.0k/mo.

Emily — great, thanks for the quick reply. Confirming next steps and timeline below so procurement/QA and our teams are aligned:

1) Eval start: Monday 2026-02-23 (we’ll provision Friday 2/20 for early access and set up test harness).
2) Deliverables before start: prompt-pack v1 (attached), benchmark CSV, and a short-run checklist for QA (shared to Drive).
3) Security/compliance: we will enforce US-only log retention for the pilot and provide S3 export ACLs — Ben will share the S3 doc and SLO exception note this afternoon.
4) Acceptance criteria for pilot success (proposed):
   - QA task accuracy (Medexa QA set): Atlas >= 92% F1; Optima >= 85% F1; Reach >= 78% F1 on short answers.
   - Latency SLOs: Optima p95 <= 300ms; Reach p95 <= 150ms.
   - No more than 3% regression on hallucination score across evaluation slices.

If this looks good, Emily — can you confirm the two points: a) procurement contact and b) whether we should include Atlas only as a gated regression runner or as part of live routing?

I’ll book a 30-min kickoff for Monday 2/23 and share the Drive folder + HubSpot update (deal HD-2026-MED-84).

Thanks — looking forward.

Aisha
